note: The package and environment half of the stack table. Capability availability, satisfaction, and evidence are the other half and live with the planner (issue #12). One table, two owners; do not duplicate a column across them.

citations.sizes_and_licenses: Hugging Face model API, read 2026-08-17 at the revision each package pins. bytes is the sum of the revision's file sizes; license_declared is the model card's own field.
citations.revisions: Recovered from the recorded runs: .cache/huggingface/download/*.metadata under each local model directory, and the hub snapshot directories for the MLX checkpoints.

license_policy: license_declared is what the model card says at the pinned revision. license_reviewed stays false until someone reads the terms; a declared license is evidence that one exists, not a redistribution clearance. `audio packages list` reports both.

core.reason: The tool's own environment: numpy, scipy, onnxruntime. Nothing to provision, and the only place small hash-pinned artifacts auto-fetch.

mlx.reason: mlx-audio 0.4.5 requires transformers >=5.5.0,<5.13.0, which nothing else here accepts. Deliberately torch-free.

guards.why: The private batched decode path Qwen's timing figures came from. Verified to match on an environment built from this lock.

torch-firered.reason: FireRed pins transformers at exactly 5.1.0. It cannot join mlx (>=5.5.0) or torch-vibevoice (<5.0.0), and mlx-audio implements no punctuator, so this stack cannot move to MLX at all: punctuated text is a floor.

torch-vibevoice.provisional_because: mlx-audio 0.4.5 runs VibeVoice-ASR with no added dependencies, at 12.4 GB peak against 20.8 GB, but produces a different transcript (47 segments against 49, some traditional-character orthography, one lexical difference). Adopting it replaces every recorded VibeVoice figure. This environment exists until that re-measurement decides.

swift.reason: A Swift build product plus one Core ML model package. No interpreter, so no lock; absent `swift` blocks only these packages and is reported by `audio doctor` rather than being fatal.

silero-vad.note: The one package that auto-fetches, because it is small and hash-pinned. Already implemented in src/audio_cli/vad.py; pull records it in the registry rather than re-downloading it.

supersedes.environment_was: a PyTorch environment via the qwen-asr package
supersedes.evidence: model_tests/benchmark/results/2026-08-17-mlx-collapse-probes.json — identical token text on all 246 aligned tokens across all 17 word-bearing segments, no punctuation-invariant violations, bound agreement median 0 s with P95 80 ms and max 1.6 s.

vibevoice-asr-7b.note: Native speaker structure, so the `diarization` capability is native on this stack and no diarizer add-on is planned for it.

firered-asr2s.note: One package supplying four roles, because the four checkpoints are provisioned and versioned together and no plan uses one without the checkout that loads it. `lid` costs a second inference pass; the punctuator always runs, because punctuated text is a floor.

fluidaudio.unsized_because: A Swift build product, whose size depends on the toolchain that builds it. pull records the measured size afterwards.
fluidaudio.note: Also ships a Core ML VAD that its own VadManager resolves. That is not a named package here: the comparison probe exercised it, but this tool has never provisioned it. If --vad fluidaudio ships, it becomes one and gets its own entry.
